news.title: Dems’ hatred of Trump created this socialist monster — and now it’s turning on them
news.text:
Voters’ “affordability” fears are supposedly fueling the Democratic Party’s new, strident socialism.

Yet annual inflation during former President Joe Biden’s four years peaked at over 9%, while prices for some key staples rose by 30% over his tenure — all to silence from the left.

The socialists weren’t just quiet during Biden’s term; they were themselves responsible for his rampant inflation.

They had implemented an inflationary de facto third Obama term, ramming through the most radical and costly agenda in decades under the veneer of Biden’s cognitively challenged waxen effigy.

So the current Jacobin takeover of the Democratic Party was not sparked by concerns about “affordability” — at least not if “affordability” means the middle-class struggle to buy a house, a car or groceries.

Instead, this socialist moment is merely the logical culmination of years of boutique radicalism within the Democratic aristocracy.

Almost every weaponized scam and national hysteria in the last two decades was amplified and spread by mainstream Democrats: the farcical claim that the Wuhan-lab-hatched COVID virus came from pangolins or bats, the deification of George Floyd, the radical diminution of in-person voting, the mythology of a 1619 national founding and more.

Who allowed over 10 million border-jumpers into the country — illegal, unvetted and instantaneously dependent on the welfare state?

Who gave us multiple genders and biological males showering with teenage girls or female prisoners?

Who sloganeered about “defund the police” and “no cash bail”?

All this was about as radical as it gets.

The Democratic establishment’s unhinged hatred of Donald Trump helped birth the socialist-cum-communist Frankensteinian monster that’s now devouring its mad-scientist creators.

“By any means necessary” was a Democratic mantra over a decade ago.

By 2016, the Democratic leadership and the Clinton campaign were hatching the Steele-dossier farce to warp an election.

In 2020, the Democratic deep state fabricated the farcical claim that the Hunter Biden laptop was Russian disinformation, a hoax that, this time around, likely did alter an election.

Then came four unhinged years of anti-Trump lawfare.

All those perversions of the legal system were accompanied by a host of mainstream Democrats, retired generals, politicos and athletes shouting that Trump was a Nazi, a fascist, a traitor or a Putin asset.

Three would-be assassins got close to killing Trump — near-death encounters that elicited unapologetic applause for the attempts.

Murderers themselves were normalized as leftist icons, as seen in the canonization of Luigi Mangione.

Yet did the establishment Democratic apparat calm these waters?

Or did it set them boiling?

It was Chuck Schumer who threatened conservative Supreme Court justices, sounding more like a pink-haired anti-ICE street protester than a US senator.

No surprise that two years later a left-wing would-be assassin turned up at Kavanaugh’s home.

Maxine Waters urged the public to bird-dog Trump administration officials and harass them whenever they were seen in public — “in a restaurant, in a department store, at a gasoline station.”

Then there was soon-to-be Vice President Kamala Harris egging on the violent George Floyd demonstrations: “This is a movement, I’m telling you . . . And everyone beware, because . . they’re not going to let up, and they should not.”

So today’s young socialists and communists did not really hijack the party: They were spawned and nurtured by aged Democrats.

They became irate over their impotence and loss of influence — and simply upgraded the methods and message of their elders.

They did not storm the party parapets, but were invited in by a party that had already radicalized itself — amid its hatred of Trump and its growing estrangement from the majority of the American people.

Socialists did not lower the bar for extremism; establishment Democrats had already destroyed that standard altogether.

The only change is that the electrified socialist monsters have awakened.

They have mocked their stagnant creators, reenergized the old messages, and now simply seek to replace the messengers.

Now, the new socialists think, hardcore leftists no longer have to hide their agendas for fear of losing elections.

In their folly, they attributed Harris’ 2024 implosion not to her clumsy efforts to disown and disguise her radical past (including the most left-wing voting record in the Senate), but to her not being left-wing enough.

In other words, they’re convinced a milquetoast socialist lost in 2024 not because she was too radical for America, but because she was not socialist — or indeed, communist — enough.

So the crazed new socialists are brazenly broadcasting the old agendas: open borders, mass amnesties, defunding the police, ending fossil fuels, seeking to destroy the Senate and Supreme Court, scapegoating whites and white “privilege” — and adding a new element, anti-Zionism and indeed antisemitism.

America will soon see how this insanity works out.

Victor Davis Hanson is a distinguished fellow of the Center for American Greatness.

news.title: Debate over trans athletes overtakes WNBA
news.text:
The WNBA has been on a meteoric rise the last few years. It's so popular it just signed media rights deals worth $3.1 billion US. 

But with that explosion in popularity and cultural cache has come the projection of larger culture war issues onto the league.

The latest? The debate over trans athletes in sports. 

It started earlier this month, when Indiana Fever sharpshooter Sophie Cunningham ignited an online firestorm after an ESPN profile quoted her voicing support for barring transgender girls and women from women's sports. 

"I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think, with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men," Cunningham said. 

The issue — which has been a major point of contention in the U.S. for more than a year now after President Donald Trump signed an executive order preventing trans people from participating in women's or girls' sporting events — remained a focal point during Tuesday's matchup between the Fever and Seattle Storm. 

Poilievre backs J.K. Rowling's support for Olympic ban of transgender women from women's sportsBreaking down the IOC policy banning transgender women from female Olympic events

Rally outside game renews controversy

Outside the arena, there was a small rally in support of Cunningham's comments and pushing for a proposal currently on the ballot in the state of Washington that would bar transgender students from competing in girls' athletics at school (the Supreme Court upheld similar laws in Idaho and West Virginia last month). 

Inside the arena, a Storm player wore a trans rights shirt ahead of playing. Cunningham was booed throughout the game, according to ESPN. And the co-owner of the Storm, Celeste Keaton, got suspended for five home games for allegedly cursing out two fans wearing t-shirts with XX and XY chromosomes in support of Cunningham. 

The Storm apologized for Keaton's comments and said in a statement: "Everyone who attends a Storm game deserves to feel welcome, and we remain committed to creating an inclusive environment where every fan is treated with respect." 

Cunningham weighed in as well, posting on social media: "Truly embarrassing of the co-owner. Unfortunately shows the type of leader she is." 

She also wrote, "I truly believe there is a safe space and love for EVERYBODY. Biological girls, biological boys, trans women, and trans men. Everyone is welcome at my table! You can disagree and still be kind." 

Scrutiny of WNBA intensifies as mounting discord around the league looms over all-star festivitiesTrump bans transgender female athletes from women's sports in new executive order

The events at the Tuesday game and Cunningham's initial comments have been fodder on Fox News. White House spokesperson Karoline Leavitt also weighed in, saying it was "astonishing" to see the backlash Cunningham was receiving from "Democrats and left-wing figures across the country." 

"Men should not be playing in women's sports. It's completely ludicrous that anyone could support that."

Politics 'a lightning rod'

Trans rights has been a longtime pet issue for the Trump White House. In the lead up to the 2024 election Trump ran an ad attacking Kamala Harris's support for gender-affirming care for trans people. The campaign focused on NFL and college football. 

"I think anything political from an athlete right now, particularly around race, around transgender issues, it's going to become a lightning rod right now," said Molly Yanity, the director of the sports media and communication program at the University of Rhode Island. She said Cunningham is particularly high profile and on social media, including Reddit, has earned the nickname "MAGA Barbie" — fair or not. 

"[Cunningham] hasn't really come out with any, let's say, progressive, kind of politics. So I think that the absence of her saying anything opens the door to assumptions that she is on the other side of that." 

U.S. Supreme Court upholds Idaho, West Virginia laws banning transgender women athletes from women's sportsMegan Rapinoe says AI flagged her as a brand 'risk' over trans rights advocacy

While the Indiana Fever came out saying neither the organization nor Cunningham had any knowledge of the demonstration at the arena Tuesday, Alejandra Caraballo, a clinical instructor at the Harvard Law Cyberlaw Clinic who frequently speaks about trans rights, sees the WNBA's suspension of the Storm's co-owner as a kind of green light for protesters to keep bringing politics to the sport. 

"They're saying they're there to support Sophie, but what they're really there to do is support a transphobic message," she said. "They're intentionally trying to go to these events to get reactions to film and create content and further this controversy and bring attention."

Not WNBA's first brush with controversy

This isn't the first time the WNBA has found itself at the nexus of American culture wars. 

Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas said she had received death threats and been called racial slurs for making contact with star player Caitlin Clark's throat during a game in June. Republican lawmakers have recently fuelled the controversy by writing a letter in early July saying they were concerned by reports that "attacks against Clark may be racially motivated." 

Yanity thinks a lot of the controversy is being drummed up by fans, not the players. And then are being discussed ad nauseum on social media. 

"It has become a very, very toxic place where threats of violence have been made against specifically the Black players." 

The league has faced criticism that they are not doing enough to protect players from the online onslaught. Last week, WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert called the online abuse "unacceptable," saying "The racism, the misogyny, the homophobia, the harassment, and threats directed to our players, has no place in sport or anywhere else."

The WNBA did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CBC.

Ultimately, said Yanity, this is a league that has seen explosive growth over the last several years. "It used to be that you'd have to search high and low to find the games. [Now] they are all readily available and at your fingertips. … These social aspects of the game are also being analyzed." 

To add to that, she said politics are inherent to women's sport, pointing to the fact that it took an act of Congress in the U.S. and a president's signature for women to even get on the court and have a somewhat even playing field. 

"Everything about a woman's existence, and particularly a Black woman's existence, is political."

news.title: Hasan Piker Makes Bold Prediction About 2028 Democratic Presidential Nominee
news.text:
Leftist Twitch streamer and activist Hasan Piker made a startling prediction about what position the 2028 Democratic nominee for president will hold on a major policy. 

In a wide-ranging interview with CNN’s Donie O’Sullivan, Piker was asked if he’d endorse the 2028 Democratic nominee, even if they supported Israel in a way that he does not like. 

“If you ultimately are about defeating fascism in this country as you describe it, surely shouldn’t you get on board with whoever the main candidate is?” O’Sullivan said. 

Piker said he doesn’t believe he will have to make that decision. 

“There is 0% chance that whoever the elected Democrat is that wins the primary will be pro-Israel in any way, shape or form. You’ll see,” Piker said. 

The issue of support for Israel has become a prominent one among Democratic voters in recent years, particularly younger voters in the wake of the Oct 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and Israel’s subsequent war in Gaza. 

Polls have found that Americans’ support for Israel is at historic lows, largely due to accusations that the country has committed genocide against the Palestinian people. 

According to the Pew Research Center, 60% of U.S. adults have an unfavorable view of Israel. 

In 2025, a United Nations commission found that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. 

The International Criminal Court also has standing arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and crimes against humanity related to the war in Gaza. 

Piker, who did not endorse former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 due to the Biden administration’s policy on the war in Gaza (Piker has said he voted for Harris), has frequently thrown his considerable influence behind democratic socialist candidates.

These include New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and New York congressional candidates Claire Valdez, Darializa Avila Chevalier and Brad Lander. The latter three won their primary elections in June. 

While these victories occurred in heavily Democratic areas, the left-leaning side of the party has gained significant influence in recent months. 

The success of these candidates has now caused a rift among Democrats over the future direction of the party — with many moderate members and lawmakers arguing the democratic socialist message is not a winning one on the national stage. 

In addition to speaking with Piker, O’Sullivan also interviewed veteran Democratic strategist James Carville for Sunday’s episode of “The Whole Story with Anderson Cooper” entitled “The Left Insurgency.” 

“I see challenges from the quote ‘progressive left’ unquote. And these people are too hardheaded to know that they’re not popular,” Carville said. “People don’t like them, they don’t win elections, they never run against Republicans, they just run against other Democrats, and their only message is we’re gonna blow everything up.”

O’Sullivan raised Carville’s point to Piker that this will all “implode at the general election.” 

“Yeah, as opposed to previous neoliberal Democratic candidacies that have been spectacular successes so far,” Piker said before referencing former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and Harris’s losses to President Donald Trump in 2016 and 2024, respectively. 

“There are a lot of people who are just like ‘this is not working’” Piker continued. “Cost of living crisis is completely out of control; Democrats haven’t done anything about it, Republicans haven’t done anything about it, there has to be a different alternative.” 

O’Sullivan’s episode of “The Whole Story with Anderson Cooper” airs on Aug. 2 at 8 p.m. ET on CNN.

news.title: New York sues Kalshi, says its prediction markets are illegal gambling
news.text: New York's attorney general sued Kalshi on Friday, claiming that its prediction market platform violates state laws against illegal gambling.In a petition filed in a state court in Manhattan, Attorney General Letitia James ‌said Kalshi failed ⁠to obtain ⁠a New York State Gaming Commission license to operate its platform, where people trade based on the predicted outcomes of events such as sports and elections.The attorney ​general said such platforms can encourage problem gambling, including by people under age 21, and endanger people's financial, emotional and physical health. She filed similar ​petitions in April against two other prediction market operators, Coinbase Financial Markets and Gemini Titan."New York's gambling laws protect children from underage betting and help combat gambling addiction," James said in a statement. "No matter what they call themselves, prediction markets like Kalshi are gambling ​platforms, plain and simple."Kalshi and lawyers who represent the New York-based company did ⁠not immediately ‌respond to requests for comment outside business hours. Prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket have soared ​in popularity since the 2024 ​U.S. presidential election, when they fared better than pollsters in predicting Republican Donald Trump's victory over ⁠Democrat Kamala Harris.Their growth has sparked a flurry of lawsuits and countersuits over the ​authority of individual U.S. states, rather than the federal government, to regulate the industry.The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission has claimed exclusive oversight, and challenged regulatory activity in at least nine states.FEDERAL JUDGE REJECTED PREEMPTIVE KALSHI LAWSUITAccording to the petition, Kalshi's platform offers what is "quintessentially gambling" because people can wager money on events whose outcomes they don't control, such as who will win the Super Bowl or the reality TV show "Big Brother."New York also objected to Kalshi letting 18- to 20-year-olds use its platform, despite a minimum age of 21 under state law for mobile sports betting."Kalshi has ‌chosen to ignore New York's gaming laws, which exist to protect consumers, prevent problematic gambling, deliver funding for critical public services, and ensure that every company plays by the same rules," New York Governor ​Kathy Hochul said in ​a statement. "This choice has consequences." James sued ⁠two days after the federal appeals court in Manhattan rejected Kalshi's request to avoid being subjected to New York's gambling laws, while it appeals a judge's refusal on July 8 to grant a preliminary injunction against the state.Kalshi had preemptively sued New ​York last October to block enforcement.U.S. District Judge Analisa Torres, however, found that the state's interests in preventing gambling addiction, preserving the integrity of sports, and avoiding a proliferation of unregulated contracts "heavily" outweighed Kalshi's interests in ensuring the primacy of federal law and avoiding "intractable" technology issues for customers. At least four states - Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada and Washington - have won court orders restricting Kalshi's activities. New York's lawsuit against Kalshi seeks a halt to its alleged unlawful conduct, the forfeiture of illegal gains, civil fines equal to triple those gains, and restitution to customers.
news.summary: New York's attorney general has sued Kalshi, alleging its prediction market platform operates illegally. The state claims Kalshi lacks a required gambling license to offer such services. This action follows similar lawsuits filed against other prediction market operators in New York. Kalshi previously sought an injunction against state enforcement but was unsuccessful. The lawsuit seeks to halt Kalshi's operations and recover illegal gains.

news.title: Kamala Harris's $8 Million Mansion Located in Neighborhood with Nearly Zero Black Residents
news.text:
Former Vice President Kamala Harris — who preaches diversity — reportedly has a new $8 million mansion located in a neighborhood with virtually no black residents.

Harris, who has talked at length about fighting racial disparities in housing and has harped on the importance of living near black people, has a new 4,000-square-foot California mansion in Point Dume, an exclusive seaside community, according to a report by Fox News.

Point Dume, which features properties including ocean views, is estimated to be home to 94 percent white and just 0.2 percent black residents as of 2019, according to the Census Bureau’s American Community Survey.

Harris’ new mansion — which she reportedly picked up for $8.15 million — includes multiple wine fridges, private golf courses, and enough parking for five vehicles.

The former vice president moving into her luxurious home in a neighborhood with essentially zero diversity comes after years of Harris lecturing the public about the importance of living near black Americans.

“When you’re at an HBCU [historically black college or university], and especially one with the size and with the history of Howard University — and also in the context of also being in D.C., which was known forever as being ‘Chocolate City’ — it just becomes about you understanding that there is a whole world of people who are like you,” Harris told the Washington Post in 2019.

Harris was recalling her experience growing up in predominantly white social circles, before she eventually attended a historically black college in a mainly black city.

“It was more, for me, about the numerosity than it was the diversity,” she added. “I grew up in a community where there were many representations of diversity. Going to Howard, there were so many [black people]! And they’re all in your age group, in your phase of life.”

Last year, two non-white surfers wrote a review of the ritzy neighborhood in which Harris recently acquired a mansion, saying, “Despite the veneer of a laid back community of surfers who are one with nature, there are barriers to access that keep most BIPOC people away.”

Alana Mastrangelo is a reporter for Breitbart News. You can follow her on Facebook and X at @ARmastrangelo, and on Instagram.

Former Vice President Kamala Harris -- who preaches diversity -- reportedly has a new $8 million mansion located in a neighborhood with virtually no black residents.

news.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger celebrates his 79th birthday showing off his iron-pumping workout, fit physique
news.text:
Arnold Schwarzenegger flaunted his legendary muscles while marking his 79th birthday.

The “Terminator” star was pictured pumping iron in what appeared to be Los Angeles in a pair of celebratory birthday pics Thursday. 

In both snapshots, he wore a black t-shirt and matching shorts, and accessorized with a gold watch and a pair of sunglasses as he displayed his massive arms for his followers.

In the caption, the “Predator” star plugged his Pump Club — a fitness community app that offers customized nutrition tracking, workout routines, and more.

“I turn 79 today. I don’t want any gifts,” he wrote in part. “Instead, my team and I are turning the fitness industry upside down.” 

Fans of the former governor of California flocked to the comments thread to gush over his ripped physique, even as he approaches 80. 

“Happy birthday, 50 years ago you were training with one of the best physiques ever and 50 years later today you are still training with one of the best physiques ever for your age!” one person remarked, while another enthused, “HBD legend!🔥” 

A third chimed in, “Health, happiness and best of life to you 🎂 You’ve inspired an entire generation and still continue to,” while a fourth wrote, “thanks for inspiring me all those years ago to follow my dream! ✨🙏” 

Schwarzenegger — whose 28-year-old son, Joseph Baena, is following in his famous dad’s footsteps with a bodybuilding career — again defied age last month, when he stepped out with much-younger girlfriend Heather Milligan.

In a rare public appearance, the couple — who began dating 14 years ago — were spotted at the Austrian World Summit in Vienna, Austria, in June.

In a photo from the event, Milligan, 51, and the “True Lies” actor were joined by former US Vice President Kamala Harris and President Alexander Van der Bellen of Austria.

The “Kindergarten Cop” actor’s fitness-themed birthday upload comes on the heels of decades of fitness accomplishments. 

In a 2023 interview, the seven-time Mr. Olympia winner admitted to struggling with body image as he ages — even despite being more fit than the “majority” of people his age.

“I kind of smile because every day I do look in a mirror and I say, ‘Yep, you suck,’” he told Howard Stern at the time. 

“When you’ve been hailed for years as this supreme body, and you have the definition and you see the veins coming down your abs, and you see veins on top of your chest and then … you roll the clock 50 years and you’re standing there and you don’t see that anymore,” he lamented. 

He added, “I never, ever thought about that when I was 30 years old or 40 years old that this [was] going to happen. It just sucks.”
news.summary: Schwarzenegger is a seven-time Mr. Olympia winner.

news.title: Charli xcx hosts fan Q&A at Chicago’s Reckless Records
news.text:
Even with Lollapalooza in full swing at Grant Park, some fans of British pop star Charli xcx found themselves inWicker Park yesterday for a conversation with fans ahead of the musician’s headlining Lollapalooza performance Friday.

Tickets to the sold-out event were an approachable $30 and included a copy of the artist’s new album.

While an ice cream truck-turned-merch-stand blared tracks off her new album “Music, Fashion, Film,” fans sang, sweated and met new friends as they stood in line outside of the Reckless Records on Milwaukee Avenue.

The first two groups of fans in line had traveled from Alabama, Miami, and New York for Lollapalooza. After hours of standing next to each other, they realized they knew mutual people on socials and said this meetup might lead to future hangouts.

Two 17-year-olds sitting on the sidewalk under a blue umbrella had been in line since 11:30 a.m. for the 3:30 p.m. event. “I’ve never seen Charli live, so this is my opportunity,” said Addison Davis. “She’s just going to do a Q&A, but it’s the closest thing I’m getting.” Davis couldn’t get tickets to Lollapalooza but said this was a moment to make the most of it.

Charli xcx’s new album, “Music, Fashion, Film,” is a departure from her sixth studio album, “Brat,” which topped charts with its synthy club tracks and became a social media phenomenon, even making an appearance in former Vice President Kamala Harris’ campaign.

The first track released from the new album, called “Rock Music,” sparked chatter online because of its heavy guitar riffs, prompting fans to wonder if the musician was moving away from danceable electronic music. But John Norat from Miami, Florida, who was standing in line for the event, had a response to some of the backlash

“There was a whole discourse about ‘the dancefloor is dead’ thing, but I think the music she’s making now is still from the dance world, but it’s rock,” Norat opined. “The most important thing about this era is the live performances and the cadence, how she carries herself on stage. She’s a rock star, and I’m just so excited.”

Victoria Adler, who was also waiting to see the pop star in person on Thursday, said she believes this album showcases Charli xcx’s deep knowledge of music. She went to two free “Music, Fashion, Film” screenings of a related film and is loving how fan focused it all feels.

“All these secret shows she’s doing that are pop-ups, it’s just refreshing in this time to see an artist as big as she is post-‘Brat’ really giving it back to the fans.”

The sold-out event inside the record shop was closed to media, and press photography was not allowed inside. Fans who had wrist bracelets and were allowed in crowded the musician, who spent nearly 40 minutes taking questions, graciously answering everything from what kind of lip gloss was in her purse to her thoughts about public transit.

She talked about how she made the album for herself, not the fans. She added that positive reception is a bonus, not the driving force behind her creativity.

Charli xcx headlines Lollapalooza Friday in one of the most female-forward lineups in the festival’s history. Fellow women headliners include Olivia Dean and Blackpink’s Jennie on Saturday and Canadian pop queen Tate McRae, J-pop star Ado and the xx’s Romy Madley Croft on Sunday.

news.title: Trump's 'twitches and glitches' alarm expert amid fresh health concerns
news.text:
Speech-language pathologist Hillary Shea is seeing a number of red flags indicating President Donald Trump's cognitive decline is getting worse.

She elaborated on what she could see, in her expertise as a clinician, on the David Pakman Show on Thursday.

"We've observed in Donald Trump what appears to be a diminished range of vocabulary, that the sort of number of words he uses has diminished over time," said Pakman. "We've seen these, what I call glitches, where when he gets a word wrong, there's a physical thing where a shoulder goes up, and he seems to almost reboot, for lack of a better term ... am I making something out of nothing, or are there clinically relevant observations that we can make here?"

Shea confirmed these are all, in fact, trouble signs.

"What's happening within the brain networks is that the brain is supposed to be regulating and suppressing unwanted motor movements," she said, noting that this isn't well developed in kids, and also deteriorates as people age. "The frontal lobe should be suppressing unwanted motor movements like those twitches."

Pakman then noted a study during the 2024 presidential campaign finding that former President Joe Biden's vocabulary only diminished slightly from years ago, and former Vice President Kamala Harris' didn't at all — but Trump's diminished significantly. "Is that clinically relevant in some way?"

"It's absolutely clinically relevant," said Shea. "That signifies that the brain deterioration in Trump is much more significant than in Biden ... his vocabulary is very repetitive. It's very monosyllabic, which sometimes is going to have to do with the fact that it's really hard for Trump to say multisyllabic words right now." His "perseveration" on topics like the 2020 election is worrisome as well, she said.

The topic then turned to the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, the dementia test Trump constantly brags about "acing" — which Shea clarified isn't really a good sign.

"If he actually got a perfect score, a 30 out of 30, it honestly tells me nothing ... even people who have dementia, who come into my office who already have a diagnosis, can still sometimes get 30 out of 30 on that test," said Shea. "So 30 out of 30 doesn't actually tell me much. The fact that he has taken it multiple times over the course of a year and a half tells me way more." What that means, she said, is "they're looking for something, whether it's decline or medication, how is he responding to medication?"

Pakman later noted that he has seen a deterioration of Trump's motor skills as well, including his inability to cap a Sharpie and fumbling with Tic Tacs at Lindsey Graham's funeral — something Shea isn't as thorough of an expert in, but which she agreed was troubling.

"The brain controls everything," said Shea. "So, fine motor control of your articulators is the same thing as fine motor control with your fingers." She noted that his handwriting has shown signs of deterioration as well. "It's not just the muscles themselves. It's the proprioception, where his body is in space and what his arms and legs and things are doing. It's visual perceptual processing. It involves more than we think. So when you have general brain decline ... everything becomes affected."
